items.title: SAP Signavio Process and Journey Modeling: what's new in the October 2026 release
items.author: danielafabbrin40
items.text:
The October 2026 release of SAP Signavio Process Modeler marks a significant step in how you model, govern, and connect process knowledge across the enterprise. At the center is a completely reimagined Process Modeler canvas, built from the ground up with a modern, AI-native modeling experience and deep integration with the SAP Signavio Process Transformation Suite. Alongside it, this release broadens AI access, strengthens process landscape visibility, and lays the structural foundation for your transformation initiatives. 
 From making AI-assisted modeling available as a Base AI capability, a beta MCP server for AI agents, and the stage one release of the Process Atom Central Repository, this release advances both the day-to-day experience of process professionals and the longer-term vision of an intelligent, interconnected process landscape. A new Process Governance Dashboard rounds out the release, giving administrators a consolidated view of workspace health, without manual audits. 
 Here is a summary of what the new October release brings to you: 
 The new SAP Signavio Process Modeler canvas 
 Starting now, the new SAP Signavio Process Modeler canvas is available to all customers, bringing a completely reimagined modeling experience designed for the next generation of process transformation. 
 It was built from the ground up around three core ideas: 
 A modern, intuitive modeling experience that helps users focus on process improvement rather than tooling 
 Embedded AI-native modeling experience where built-in intelligence guides you from the first element to a ready-to-use process model 
 Deep integration with the SAP Signavio Process Transformation Suite, connecting process design with governance, collaboration, and insights for a more actionable view of transformation 

 *Please note that the new canvas is off by default at GA. Administrators must activate it and assign user groups before anyone can see or use it. Find out how in the activation guide handbook. 
 Read the full story in our dedicated blog post . 

 AI-assisted Process Modeler Now Included in Base AI 
 Effective October 5 th 2026, AI-assisted Process Modeler moves from a Premium AI feature to a Base AI capability for all SAP Signavio Process Modeler customers. No AI units required, no activation through SAP for Me. Workspace administrators can enable it directly within SAP Signavio AI Services settings, making it easier than ever to roll out AI-enabled process modeling across the organization. 
 For teams already using the feature, nothing changes in how it works: usage simply no longer consumes AI units. For those exploring it for the first time, AI-assisted Process Modeler lets your users generate process diagrams from text descriptions, images, and tables in just a few clicks, reducing modeling effort and making process documentation more accessible to a broader range of contributors. A fair usage limit is expected to apply at the workspace level. 

 Find out how to activate AI capabilities in your workspace and assign users in this SAP Help Portal post. 

 Turn your process data into a knowledge source for any AI agent with the SAP Signavio MCP Server (Beta) 
 Equip AI agents to answer natural language questions about your processes, build custom use cases on top of your process information, and accelerate AI-driven transformation, all through a standardized MCP (Model Context Protocol) connector that works with the AI tools your teams already use. No custom development. No dedicated connectors. 
 Want to learn how to get started w ith the SAP Signavio MCP server? You can find the step-by-step in our dedicated guide here . 

 Stage One Release of Process Atom Central Repository 
 Process knowledge today is fragmented. Defined in one place, rediscovered in another, and often lost along the way. The Process Atom Central Repository changes that by establishing a single, governed home for Process Atoms: reusable units of process behavior that teams and AI agents can build on together. 
 This Stage One Release delivers the foundational layer, introducing the Process Atom as a structured, entitled object with a central browsable repository and a basic publishing lifecycle. It focuses on establishing the core building block on which governance, AI-assisted authoring, and broader suite capabilities will follow. 

 If you’re interested in learning more about the rest of the new features of the SAP Signavio October release, check out the blog posts below: 
 SAP Signavio October 2026 Release Highlights 
 The new SAP Signavio Process Modeler canvas 
 Process Analysis and Mining 
 New AI capabilities and enhancements 
 Process Transformation Management and Collaboration 
 Process Governance

items.title: SAP Signavio Ocotber 2026 Product Release - Process Transformation Management and Process Governance
items.author: janefu
items.text:
SAP Signavio October 2026 Product Release - Process Transformation Management 
 I'm excited to share the latest innovations for process transformation management and process governance as part of our SAP Signavio October 2026 product release! 
 Fresh off the SAP Transformation Excellence Summit in Berlin, where we explored how organizations can accelerate transformation and turn AI-powered insights into measurable business outcomes, this release brings several exciting innovations to help you do just that. From turning AI-generated recommendations into actionable transformation initiatives to tracking realized business value and continuously enriching initiatives with the latest insights, these enhancements help organizations move faster from insight to execution, keep transformation efforts on track, and demonstrate tangible business impact. 
 Let's take a closer look at what's new! 
 SAP Signavio Process Transformation Manager 
 Turn AI recommendations into action, track realized transformation value, and keep initiatives execution-ready. 
 Turn AI-powered recommendations into actionable transformation initiatives 
 Identifying process improvement opportunities is only the beginning. The real value comes from turning those insights into action. Transformation leads can now use the Process Consulting Agent to create actionable initiatives and supporting insights directly from AI-generated process optimization recommendations. When Process Consultaingn Agent identifies an improvement opportunity, your users can seamlessly turn the recommendation into structured transformation content while preserving the underlying process context, rationale, and supporting findings. This helps you bridge the gap between process analysis and execution planning without the need to manually recreate information. The same also extends to value management. Process Consulting Agent can use relevant findings from SAP Signavio Process Intelligence or user-provided business information to create structured manual value cases, helping teams connect identified improvement opportunities with expected business value. Key benefits include: 
 Accelerate insights to action: Turn AI-generated optimization recommendations into actionable transformation initiatives and insights with less manual effort. 
 Preserve valuable context: Keep supporting process findings, rationale, and recommendations connected to transformation work. 
 Streamline transformation planning: Create structured initiatives and insights directly from AI recommendations, reducing reliance on disconnected documents and manual processes. 
 Build on existing transformation work: Use existing transformation content as context to align new recommendations with ongoing initiatives and reduce duplication. 
 Connect process improvement to business value: Create manual value cases from Process Intelligence findings or user-provided inputs so improvement opportunities can be assessed and prioritized based on expected value. 

 Click here to watch the video demo for this feature 

 Keep transformation initiatives up to date with AI-assisted initiative enricher 
 Transformation doesn't stand still, and neither should your initiatives. As new process insights, business priorities, and improvement opportunities emerge, transformation teams need to continuously adapt their initiatives without duplicating work or starting from scratch. 
 With the new Initiative Enricher for AI-Assisted Transformation Advisory, transformation leads can enhance existing initiatives directly within SAP Signavio Process Transformation Manager. AI analyzes an initiative's existing insights, assets, and tasks, identifies where additional context could improve the recommendations, and proposes relevant new attributes, assets, and tasks. Suggested content is displayed alongside existing information, making it easy to identify what's new and avoid duplication. Importantly, you remain in full control. Every AI-generated suggestion can be individually reviewed and approved before adding to the initiative, ensuring you stay in control and understand where each recommendation comes from. Key benefits include: 
 Continuously strengthen initiatives: Enrich existing initiatives with relevant attributes, assets, and tasks without recreating work already in progress. 
 Identify opportunities for improvement: Receive AI-assisted guidance on missing information and additional context that could strengthen an initiative. 
 Avoid duplication: Compare proposed enhancements with existing initiative content before deciding what to add. 
 Maintain transparency and control: Review and selectively approve AI-generated suggestions, with clear visibility into their sources and attribution. 
 By making it easier to continuously enrich transformation work, this innovation helps you and your teams to keep initiatives relevant, actionable, and execution-ready as business needs evolve. 

 Track realized transformation value and demonstrate measurable business impact 
 Transformation success isn't just about identifying opportunities or estimating potential benefits. It's about demonstrating the value that has actually been achieved. With the latest value tracking and realization feature in SAP Signavio Process Transformation Manager, transformation leads can now capture, monitor, and visualize realized business value alongside expected value throughout the transformation lifecycle. 
 The capability supports both manually created value cases and value cases originating from SAP Signavio Process Intelligence, providing a more consistent approach to tracking business outcomes across transformation initiatives. Realized values can be entered manually or automatically synchronized from source systems where supported, giving teams the flexibility to track outcomes while maintaining transparency into the underlying data. New historical trend visualizations also make it easier to understand how realized value progresses over time, compare results against expected targets, and identify deviations that may require attention. Key benefits include: 
 Demonstrate measurable business impact: Track actual realized value alongside expected value to clearly distinguish planned benefits from achieved outcomes. 
 Enable end-to-end value tracking: Monitor business value from initial opportunity identification through execution to realized results across manual and system-sourced value cases. 
 Visualize value progression: Track historical value trends to understand progress toward targets, identify deviations, and support timely decisions. 
 Simplify value tracking and reporting: Automatically synchronize realized values from Process Insights and Process Intelligence when available, while enabling manual updates when needed. 
 Ensure data transparency and flexibility: Maintain source-system linkage and distinguish synchronized from manually adjusted values for more reliable reporting. 
 Strengthen transformation steering: Equip transformation teams and stakeholders with actionable insights to assess initiative performance, prioritize improvements, and demonstrate transformation success. 
 With this you can now move beyond measuring transformation potential to actually demonstrating tangible business results. 

 Click here to watch the video demo for this feature 

 Manage transformation tasks with greater flexibility and control 
 Successful transformation requires more than well-defined initiatives. It also depends on clear responsibilities, effective collaboration, and the ability to keep execution on track. The enhanced suite tasks experience introduces additional capabilities to help users manage transformation tasks more efficiently across SAP Signavio Process Transformation Suite. With new task attributes, including due dates, as well as enhanced filtering and sorting capabilities, users can better organize their work, identify priorities, and stay on top of upcoming deadlines. More granular access management also provides greater flexibility in controlling who can view or edit individual tasks, helping teams collaborate while maintaining appropriate permissions. Key benefits include: 
 Stay on top of priorities: Set task due dates and use enhanced filtering and sorting capabilities to organize work and manage deadlines. 
 Improve task visibility: Access additional task attributes for a clearer understanding of responsibilities and execution progress. 
 Gain greater control: Manage access at the individual task level with more granular permissions. 
 Support effective collaboration: Enable a more transparent, flexible, and scalable task management experience across transformation initiatives. 

 Click here and here to watch the video demos for this feature 
 Other Enhancements: 
 Beyond these innovations, the October release introduces further improvements to help transformation teams connect strategic objectives, process insights, and execution activities. 
 Visualize relationships between transformation initiatives and objectives: Gain a clearer understanding of how transformation initiatives contribute to strategic business goals with a new visual relationship graph in SAP Signavio Process Transformation Manager. By making connections between initiatives and their associated objectives visible, teams can more easily navigate transformation work, understand strategic alignment, and see how individual initiatives support broader transformation priorities. 
 Convert correction recommendations into transformation insights: Move more seamlessly from process analysis to transformation planning by converting data-driven correction recommendations from SAP Signavio Process Insights into structured insights in SAP Signavio Process Transformation Manager. This enhancement enables transformation leads to preserve important analytical findings and connect them to relevant transformation work, reducing manual effort while maintaining the context behind each recommendation. 

 Continue your transformation journey with SAP Signavio 
 You direct, AI executes. Realize value across your process transformation journey. The October 2026 release brings this vision to life, empowering organizations to accelerate transformation with AI while keeping people in control. From AI-powered recommendations to actionable initiatives and measurable business outcomes, SAP Signavio Process Transformation Manager helps teams move seamlessly from insight to execution and value realization. 
 Want to know what else is coming out as part of this release? Check out our highlight blog for SAP Signavio Process Transformation Suite and find out what else we have coming out this month!

items.title: What's New in SAP Subscription Billing (Q3 2026)
items.author: SvenjaMS
items.text:
This edition of our quarterly series highlighting the latest improvements in SAP Subscription Billing covers a range of updates, from flexible subscription onboarding and smarter pricing logic to enhanced data privacy controls and more granular billing configuration. Read on to see what's new and how these changes can benefit your business. 

 Phased Subscription Onboarding with Subscription Ramps 
 Bringing new customers onto a subscription often works better when conditions are introduced gradually — lower prices or reduced quantities at the start, stepping up over time as the customer realizes full value. Subscription ramps make this possible by letting you define successive phases within a subscription, each with its own conditions, as agreed in a ramp deal. 
 Each ramp period can specify a different combination of: 
 Product 
 Product price (via rate plan or customized prices and discounts) 
 Product quantity (via subscription parameters for license-based subscriptions) 
 Ramp periods are stored as snapshots. The item list in the Manage Subscriptions app has been redesigned to give you a clear overview of all snapshots at a glance, without needing to switch views. 

 The fields displayed in the item list depend on the ramp profile configured in the Manage Business Configuration app under Subscription Settings : 

 You can create up to 10 ramp periods per subscription. Ramp periods are always adjacent to each other without gaps or overlaps. Once the last ramp period ends, its conditions remain in effect until a new snapshot is created. Key capabilities 
 Create ramp periods during subscription creation or while the subscription is in a pending state 
 Adjust the length of ramp periods (pending subscriptions only) 
 Edit ramp period content in effective subscriptions, including splitting a period to apply different conditions for part of it 
 Delete individual or all ramp periods while the subscription is pending Example 
 A rolling subscription for a printer has two initial 6-month ramp periods with decreasing discounts on the price per copy. The third ramp period defines the longer-term conditions with no discount. After the last ramp period ends, those conditions remain valid. 

 For full details, see Subscription Ramps . 

 Bill Consolidation Control at Subscription Level 
 You can now configure bill splitting directly in billing profiles using the new Split Bills by Subscription setting in the Manage Business Configuration app. When this setting is active, each subscription produces its own bill. Charges from different subscriptions are never merged, even when other aggregation criteria would normally combine them. 

 The setting is also visible in the Manage Billing Data app on the General Info tab of the billing profile: 

 This is particularly useful when customers require itemized billing per subscription for internal cost allocation, auditing, or contractual reasons. Example 
 A corporate customer has multiple active subscriptions for different departments. With Split Bills by Subscription enabled, each department receives a separate bill for its own subscription, simplifying internal chargebacks. 

 Working Directly with Amounts in Pricing Logic 
 Pricing logic can now handle monetary amounts natively. You can calculate amounts, use them in conditional logic, and return them as price elements, all within a single price element specification. A new amount field type is available in the Manage Field Catalog app. Amount fields can be included in lookup tables and either returned directly as a price or passed on as a property to subsequent components in the pricing tree. 
 Three new pricing tree components support this: 
 Amount Calculation: Calculates an amount based on a price condition. 
 Amount Comparison: Compares two monetary amount fields (or one against the reference price property) and branches logic based on the result. 
 Set Price Element: Returns an amount field as a price element. 
 There are three new components you can use to calculate amounts and build pricing logic based on them: 
 Operator: Amount Calculation 
 This component is used to calculate an amount which you can then use in subsequent steps of the pricing tree. 
 Comparator: Amount Comparison 
 This component compares the values of a monetary amount field to another one, or to the reference price property. It decides on different action paths depending on the result. 
 Function: Set Price Element 
 This component is the pricing tree component used to generate a price element by returning an amount field. 
 Amount fields can be defined as output fields in lookup tables, making them accessible via the Table Lookup component. Furthermore, amount fields can be used within the Execute Formula component for further calculation before returning a price element. 
 Results, including amount fields, are visible in the Analyze Pricing Documents app. Example 
 A pricing rule applies a flat monthly fee stored in a lookup table, adjusted by a multiplier based on the customer's contracted tier. The Amount Calculation component handles the multiplication, and Set Price Element returns the result directly as a charge. 
 To find out more, see Pricing Tree . 

 Volume-Based Discounts on Usage Events and Transactions 
 You can now define prices based on the number of usage events or transactions, represented by the count of usage records. The standard fields cumulativeUsageCount and usageCount are now available for this purpose in your pricing configuration. 
 During usage rating, the number of usage records is determined and passed to the billing process. In the Manage Billing Data app, the consumed usage record count is displayed in the new Usage Count field. If cross-billing cycle aggregation is in use, a second Usage Count field is shown for the aggregated value. Example 
 A bike rental provider wants to apply a volume discount only when customers meet two thresholds within a billing cycle: 
 Monthly ride count: The number of individual rides taken (usage record count) 
 Monthly spend threshold: The total value of those rides (aggregated quantity) 
 The discount is applied only when both thresholds are met. Using usageCount for the ride count and cumulativeUsageCount for the aggregated spend across billing cycles, the provider can configure a two-dimensional pricing rule. The resulting discount is calculated during usage rating and is visible to the customer on their bill. 

 Data Retention and Deletion Policies per Legal Entity 
 Managing data privacy across multiple legal entities within a single SAP Subscription Billing tenant is now more precise. You can configure data retention rules per company code, using SAP Subscription Billing's integration with the next-generation SAP Data Privacy Integration service. What this enables 
 Define multiple business purposes within the same tenant, for example, separate purposes for individual customers and corporate customers per company. 

 Configure retention rules per combination of data controller (company code), data subject role (individual customer or corporate customer), and information lifecycle management object type (customer, subscription, or bill), with separate residence and retention periods for each object type. 

 Use company code as the anchor for data protection processes, ensuring deletion and retention are applied per legal entity. 
 To include customers and business documents in deletion processes, a company code must be maintained on all relevant records. 
 In the Manage Business Configuration app, company mapping is now configurable on the Markets tab: Example 
 A subscription business operating in both Germany and the United States needs to apply different retention periods for customer data in each jurisdiction. With company code-based retention rules, each legal entity's data is governed independently within the same tenant. 
 For full details on data protection in SAP Subscription Billing, see Data Protection and Privacy . 

 Billing in Advance Configurable Directly in Subscriptions 
 Managing recurring charges that are billed both in advance and in arrears previously required separate rate plans for each combination. You can now reduce that overhead by enabling users to set the Billing in Advance option directly at the subscription item level. To enable this, define the Billing in Advance setting as a parameter in a rate plan template. In any subscription item using a rate plan based on that template, users can then override the default value, choosing advance or arrears billing as needed, without requiring a separate rate plan. 
 The setting appears on the item-level Billing tab in the Manage Subscriptions app, using the parameter label defined in the rate plan template. Example 
 A company offers a software subscription that is typically billed in arrears, but certain enterprise customers prefer billing in advance for budget planning purposes. Rather than maintaining two separate rate plans, the subscription manager simply sets the billing preference at the subscription item level. 

 Pricing Configuration Apps Now Available in SAP Build Work Zone 
 A quick but useful update: the pricing configuration apps are now accessible in the SAP Build Work Zone, standard edition interface. For more information, see Integration with SAP Build Work Zone, standard edition . 

 This wraps up the Q3 2026 update for SAP Subscription Billing. As always, the goal behind these features is to give you more flexibility and control, whether that's in how you onboard customers, structure your pricing, or manage compliance across entities. 
 We'll be back at the end of Q4 with an overview of the latest features. Until then, keep innovating!

items.title: How do you handle missing exchange rates without compromising financial reporting?
items.author: suryacreatx
items.text:
Hi everyone, 
 I've been thinking about a scenario that can easily become a data-quality issue in SAP Finance reporting. 
 Imagine we're building a Finance analytical model in SAP Datasphere. We have transaction amounts in different currencies, and we need to convert them into a common reporting currency using exchange rates from TCURR . 
 Now consider this scenario: 
 A transaction is posted on 15 October in USD. 

 The reporting currency is EUR. 

 The model looks for the applicable USD-to-EUR exchange rate for that date. 

 The required rate isn't available in the exchange-rate data. 
 What should happen next? 
 We could leave the converted amount empty, flag the transaction for investigation, or use the most recent available rate. Each approach has different implications for reporting accuracy. 
 Using the previous available rate might seem practical, but it could also produce a misleading financial figure if the business expects the rate valid for the transaction date. 
 I'm curious how others handle this in SAP Datasphere and S/4HANA Finance implementations. 

 Do you fail validation when the required exchange rate is missing, or allow the model to continue with a flagged amount? 

 If you use the previous available rate, how do you validate it and prevent an outdated rate from being used indefinitely? 

 Where do you implement this logic: during data preparation, in the graphical view, or in the analytical model? 

 How do you distinguish a genuinely missing rate from a rate that exists under a different exchange-rate type or quotation convention? 
 I'd particularly like to hear about approaches that preserve financial accuracy while keeping reporting models maintainable. 
 Thanks!

items.title: Keep manual “Identification” value in payment media management after activating J78
items.author: AlvaroFernandezMorales
items.text:
Dear community; 
 We are working with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Until now, in the Manage Automatic Payments app, users created a payment parameter and manually filled in the “Identification” field with free text (date, currency, etc.) to identify the payment run. That text was then carried over to the payment media management app, where it was used to recognize it. 
 After activating scope item J78 (Advanced Cash Operations), what is entered in the parameter no longer reaches the payment media management app, and the field is now populated automatically with a value generated by SAP. Users have lost traceability of their payment runs. 
 Our questions are: 
 Is there any configuration or parameter to deactivate the automatic population of this field by SAP and keep the text entered by the user? 
 If not, is there a standard way to fill in a field when creating the payment proposal (reference, free text or other) so that it is visible later in the payment media management app? 
 Any experience or recommendation would be appreciated. 
 Thanks in advance.

Starting in October, SAP is expanding the Stay Certified experience with new ways for certified professionals to demonstrate current knowledge, including AI-powered roleplays grounded in real-world customer scenarios. 

 What the cloud introduced, AI has only accelerated: constant software updates, new capabilities, and a faster pace of innovation. For professionals working across the SAP ecosystem, keeping pace with that change is becoming an increasingly important part of maintaining their expertise. 

 For consultants, developers, architects, project managers, and sales and presales professionals, staying current means understanding not only what has changed, but how those changes apply in their work and in the customer situations they encounter. 
 Validate your SAP expertise with performance-based credentials built for the AI era 

 Learn more 

 SAP Certification has evolved alongside this changing technology landscape. As cloud solutions introduced faster release cycles, regular Stay Certified assessments became part of the certification journey, helping professionals keep their knowledge and credentials current. 

 Building on this evolution, SAP is reimagining the Stay Certified experience. Across more than 100 certifications, certified professionals will have greater choice in how they demonstrate that their knowledge remains current. Alongside a knowledge-based assessment option, learners will be able to complete short, practical, AI-powered roleplays designed around real-world customer interactions. 

 From a stand-alone assessment quiz to scenario-based roleplays 

 The evolution of Stay Certified reflects a broader shift already taking place across SAP Certification: moving beyond assessing what someone knows toward validating how they can apply that knowledge. 

 AI-powered roleplays bring that principle into the annual certification renewal experience. 

 Rather than only responding to questions about SAP products and capabilities, learners can work through simulated customer interactions built around defined knowledge goals. The scenarios are grounded in content reflecting the latest SAP product releases, helping learners demonstrate applied, up-to-date knowledge. After each assessment, learners also receive immediate, personalized feedback highlighting what went well and where they can improve, specific to the scenario rather than a generic score. 

 Learners who prefer or require a non-AI pathway will continue to have the option of completing a stand-alone assessment quiz. 

 Keeping pace with SAP innovation 

 As SAP products evolve, so does the knowledge required to work with them effectively. 

 The reimagined Stay Certified approach is designed to keep renewal closely aligned with those developments. Assessments are grounded in content reflecting the latest SAP product releases, helping learners focus on the knowledge and capabilities that have changed since getting certified or the latest certification renewal. 

 For professionals, this creates a clearer connection between maintaining a credential and maintaining relevant expertise. For customers, this means credentials can continue to reflect hands-on, up-to-date expertise aligned with current SAP product capabilities. 

 The approach builds on the broader evolution of SAP Certification toward practical, skills-based validation. SAP has expanded certification beyond traditional multiple-choice exams to include practical, performance-based assessments designed to validate how professionals apply their expertise. 

 Stay Certified now brings more of that same focus on application into the ongoing certification journey, alongside greater flexibility in managing certification renewal. A new 90-day Stay Certified renewal window will allow learners to pass their Stay Certified assessment within the 90-day window, and their certification continues seamlessly based on the original expiry date. Personalized, time-bound reminders will help learners understand when action is required, while improvements within the My Learning section on the SAP Learning site will provide clearer visibility into renewal deadlines and certification expiry. 

 Bringing hands-on validation to SAP TechEd 

 SAP is also exploring how other practical learning experiences can play a greater role in staying certified. 

 At SAP TechEd in Berlin , SAP will pilot an event-based approach that allows eligible learners to fulfill their Stay Certified requirement through participating in on-site, hands-on sessions. 

 The approach reflects the same principle behind the new roleplay assessments: practical product knowledge counts. Participation in hands-on sessions can be credited toward certification renewal, providing another way for learners to demonstrate current knowledge. 

 Staying certified in an era of continuous change 

 Earning a certification represents an important milestone. In a technology environment that changes continuously, however, expertise cannot remain static. 

 New releases, capabilities, and AI-powered ways of working mean professionals need to continually revisit what they know, understand what has changed, and apply that knowledge in new contexts. 

 Reimagined Stay Certified brings that principle more directly into certification renewal. 

 AI-powered roleplays and the hands-on pilot at SAP TechEd expand the ways learners can demonstrate practical, up-to-date knowledge as part of the Stay Certified experience. 

 As SAP technology continues to evolve, staying certified is about more than maintaining a credential. It is about demonstrating that the expertise behind it continues to evolve, too. 

 Diana Alexandra Roesner is head of Certification Transformation at SAP.

items.title: The Suite Advantage: Why Enterprises Don’t Evaluate CRM in Isolation
items.author: Binod Negi
items.text:
There is a persistent assumption in enterprise software procurement that a CRM evaluation is, at its core, a sales and service productivity decision. 
 Harmonize your CRM and CX with a single autonomous system 

 Learn how 

 You benchmark features, compare pricing, run a proof of concept, and choose the platform your sales team finds most intuitive. The ERP conversation happens in a different room, with different stakeholders, on a different cycle. 

 This separation feels logical on an org chart. In practice, it is one of the most costly fictions in enterprise technology planning. 

 The enterprise reality 

 CRM doesn’t operate in a vacuum. It operates inside a business that already has a system of record, one that holds pricing rules, credit limits, inventory positions, order histories, contract terms, and fulfillment status. That system is the ERP. When CRM and ERP are evaluated and deployed independently, the downstream consequence is not just a technical integration challenge. It is a structural gap in the information available to every customer-facing employee, every day, in every interaction that matters. 

 When CRM and ERP are built on separate data models, integration becomes a permanent overhead. Sales reps without ERP data access spend an estimated 20 to 30% of their selling time on non-selling activities such as sourcing pricing approvals, checking inventory availability, or validating order status–work that should happen automatically in the background of a connected system. The sales motion slows. Forecast accuracy degrades. And the promised ROI of the CRM investment erodes quietly, deal by deal. 

 According to Gartner® Peer Insights™ responses to the question, “What were the key factors that drove your decision?”, based on the response of actual users, 49% of SAP Sales Cloud users and 43% of SAP Service Cloud users cited pre-existing relationships as a deciding factor in their purchase decision. This is more than double the market average of about 20%. 

 At first glance, this looks like vendor loyalty. We believe it is something more deliberate than that. 

 Source: Gartner Peer Insights, SAP Sales Cloud, Sales Force Automation Platforms (Transitioning to CRM Sales Platforms) , as of Sep 18, 2026, based on 61 reviews (SAP Sales Cloud) and 508 reviews (market average). 
 Source: Gartner Peer Insights, SAP Service Cloud, CRM Customer Engagement Centre , as of Sep 18, 2026, based on 40 reviews (SAP Service Cloud) and 763 reviews (market average). 

 What native integration unlocks 

 Pre-existing relationships in enterprise software carry specific, quantifiable value. When an organization already runs SAP S/4HANA, choosing SAP Sales Cloud and SAP Service Cloud means working within a known data architecture rather than building a bridge between two foreign systems. The integration patterns are pre-established. The master data such as customers, products, pricing conditions etc is already structured in a way SAP products understand natively. The implementation risk profile is fundamentally different from deploying a point-solution CRM and then spending months, and significant budget, building and maintaining connectors to the ERP back-end. This is not loyalty to a logo. It is a rational assessment of where integration risk lives. 

 The outcomes that follow from this architectural alignment are measurable. Customers running SAP S/4HANA and SAP Sales Cloud together have achieved a 38% reduction in sales cycle duration, a 12% increase in opportunity win rate, and 42% automation of previously manual sales processes . These numbers are not the result of superior user experience alone. They are the result of sales processes that can draw on real-time ERP data like current inventory, live pricing, or credit exposure, without requiring the sales rep to leave the CRM, make a phone call, or wait for a nightly data sync. The integration is the mechanism of the outcome, not a supporting feature of it. 

 Many enterprises rely on disparate point solutions for marketing, sales, commerce, and service. Stitching these together with custom middleware and integrations is not just expensive, it’s fragile. Organizations have entire teams dedicated to building and maintaining integrations, manually transferring data between systems, and firefighting connectivity issues. The result is poor customer experiences, delayed insights, and limited scalability. 

 According to an Enterprise Strategy Group Economic Validation study , organizations that natively connect SAP CX solutions with SAP ERP unlock five compelling economic benefits: 

 Native iFlows and prebuilt connectors reduce integration and middleware costs by 25 to 80%, delivering six- to seven-figure savings over five years. 

 Seamless front-to-back connectivity drives revenue growth through higher customer registrations, improved retention, better sales conversion rates, and larger deal sizes; projecting a 30 to 441% revenue uplift over five years. 

 AI-driven automation and elimination of manual handoffs boost productivity by 25 to 90% across every stage of the sales cycle, from marketing to service. 

 Organizations go live and begin realizing customer experience improvements in as few as six months, significantly faster than point-solution alternatives. 

 Built-in compliance support reduces regulatory risk without custom development. 

 Together, these benefits deliver a validated five-year ROI of 214% to 726%. 

 Validation from our customers 

 This director of Customer Service and Support in the consumer goods industry highlights Integration and reliability strengths of SAP Sales Cloud: 
 Director of Customer Service and Support in the Consumer Goods Industry gives SAP Sales Cloud 5/5 Rating in Gartner Peer Insights™ Sales Force Automation Platforms (Transitioning to CRM Sales Platforms) Market. Read the full review here: https://gtnr.io/CFE8ZXdbP #gartnerpeerinsights 

 This marketing manager in the retail industry highlights the seamless integration enabling customer service teams to enhance customer experience: 
 Marketing Manager in the Retail Industry gives SAP Service Cloud 4/5 Rating in Gartner Peer Insights™ CRM Customer Engagement Centre Market. Read the full review here: https://gtnr.io/b8jnc45Cc #gartnerpeerinsights 

 Suite advantage is a strategic choice, not a convenience 

 SAP continues to invest in tighter, event-driven integration between these platforms, moving away from batch replication toward real-time, API-first connectivity. The adoption of SAP Integration Suite pre-built integration packages, combined with RISE with SAP and SAP GROW bundling, is lowering the barrier for customers to activate these scenarios out of the box. For organizations on the path to an intelligent enterprise, the integration between SAP S/4 HANA and SAP Sales Cloud and SAP Service Cloud integration is no longer a project, it is a product. 

 CRM value is not created in isolation, it is created at the intersection of customer data and operational data, of sales motion and business process, of pipeline intelligence and ERP reality. For organizations already running SAP, that intersection is not something to build. It is something to activate.

items.title: Back to the Future: 30 Years of SAP TechEd
items.author: Jeanette Rohr
items.text:
From SAP R/3 and the first hands-on sessions to SAP HANA, the cloud, and AI, SAP TechEd has spent three decades tracking technological change—and, at times, anticipating what was to come. 
 SAP TechEd in 2026: Join the premier technical event to build what matters 

 Register now 

 The story began in 1996, when around 700 developers and technical experts gathered in Orlando, Florida, to explore a new generation of enterprise software. 

 “It wasn’t called ‘TechEd’ back then,” explained Karl Kessler, vice president of Product Management for ABAP AI at SAP, who attended the Orlando event as a product manager for SAP Technology. “It was originally called the SAP Technical Developers Conference.” 

 The event came at a time of technological change. SAP was opening up new ways to make SAP R/3 business processes accessible over the internet. BAPI programming interface provided access to SAP business logic through defined interfaces, while ALE made it easier to exchange messages between distributed systems. SAP was also working on a “business framework” designed to integrate distributed business processes. 

 This raised a question that seems obvious today: how could enterprise software evolve into a platform for an increasingly connected IT landscape? 

 From technical training to hands-on experience 

 The event gave developers an opportunity to explore these new possibilities. But its format was still a far cry from the multifaceted platform for knowledge sharing, experimentation, and community that SAP TechEd would become over the following three decades. 

 “In the beginning, it was all very academic,” Kessler recalled. “There were no keynotes or product demos on big stages. We went straight into an introduction to the architecture of SAP R/3, and the program consisted mainly of lectures: less conference spectacle, more technical classroom.” 

 The second event, held in Los Angeles later in 1996, offered a glimpse of how quickly the SAP ecosystem was evolving. SAP and Microsoft showcased new possibilities involving Internet Explorer, SQL Server, and Microsoft Office 97. Hands-on sessions were introduced for the first time, giving participants the opportunity to work with SAP software themselves. 

 “And ‘hands-on’ really meant getting your hands dirty back then,” Kessler emphasized. “Participants had to install the software on their own laptops. Ready-to-use images that you can deploy in just a few clicks today? Not a chance.” 

 For the first time, participants had access to a software environment where they could experiment for themselves—something that has since become a staple of SAP TechEd. 

 Where technology meets community 

 In the years that followed, this shift continued. With the introduction of SAP NetWeaver, technologies like Java, portals, the web, and XML became increasingly prominent alongside the traditional ABAP world. SAP TechEd was evolving from an event where technology was explained into a place where developers could try it out and discuss it for themselves. 

 The community, too, began to play a bigger role. The SAP Developer Network created new opportunities for exchange: knowledge was no longer shared only from the stage, but also between sessions, online, and across company boundaries. 

 Kessler witnessed this evolution firsthand. From 1996 until the onset of the pandemic, he attended every SAP TechEd event in the U.S. and Europe. He initially took part as a product manager and speaker, later helping shape the program as a track lead and, for several years, an agenda lead. 

 Throughout the 2000s, SAP TechEd increasingly became a community experience. Kessler has particularly vivid memories of the events in Las Vegas: “During the day, there were lectures and four-hour hands-on sessions. But the day didn’t end when the official program did. People went out for dinner together, saw shows, or met up at the hotel in the evening. Many of us were there for practically a whole week. And if we had time afterward, we might take a trip to the Grand Canyon or Death Valley.” 

 By then, SAP TechEd had become much more than a conference program. Alongside the technical content, it was the encounters, conversations, and shared experiences that helped shape the community. 

 New formats emerged from around 2000 onward, further strengthening that community spirit. Demo Jam gave developers a stage to showcase what they had built. The Community Clubhouse created space for conversations beyond traditional presentations. Roadmap sessions offered a look at the SAP technologies to come, while hands-on sessions turned attendees from listeners into active participants. 

 “Over time, exchanging ideas became at least as important as the technology itself,” Kessler recalled. “The more complex the topics became, the more important it was to share experiences, try things out together, and learn from one another.” 
 Photo courtesy Karl Kessler 

 Technology was no longer simply presented. It was explored, discussed, and developed further–together. 

 When the future becomes the present 

 Throughout the 2000s, the technological foundations of enterprise software continued to evolve. Initially, the focus had been on connecting SAP systems with other applications through open interfaces and web technologies. Increasingly, however, a different question came to the fore: what if vast amounts of data could be made available almost in real time, without having to move and process them so extensively first? 

 Around 2010, SAP TechEd brought this idea to life. Vishal Sikka introduced SAP HANA and in-memory computing, an approach that processes data directly in main memory. It challenged established assumptions about database performance. Initially focused on analyzing large volumes of data, SAP HANA later became a foundation for applications as well. 
 Photo courtesy Karl Kessler 

 For SAP TechEd, this marked another step forward. The event was no longer just about learning new technologies; it was also about exploring their potential and understanding what they could mean in practice. An idea that had once sounded like science fiction became the starting point for new applications and business processes. 

 “It was the transition from ‘What if?’ to ‘This is how we do it,’” Kessler said. 

 Meanwhile, the community continued to evolve. The SAP Mentor program gave particularly engaged community members a new role as sounding boards, ambassadors, and representatives of the wider community. Technology and people were evolving together. 

 “Not every prediction from back then came true exactly as expected,” Kessler reflected. “Some ideas disappeared, while others developed in completely different ways. But time and again, concepts that had sounded futuristic at SAP TechEd went on to become part of everyday working life.” 

 With SAP Fiori, SAP S/4HANA, and the cloud, new topics arrived at SAP TechEd that would go on to shape the SAP landscape. Developers could experience and discuss how enterprise software was changing—and what those changes meant for their own work. 

 The focus was no longer just on what a system could do technically. Increasingly, the questions were about how enterprise software should be used: on which devices, through which interfaces, with what data, and with how much flexibility. 

 The future was becoming more tangible. It was no longer confined to architecture diagrams and technical concepts; it was visible on screens, in mobile applications, and in cloud environments. 

 At SAP TechEd, these changes were not just presented but explored and developed further together. What once opened up new possibilities became an integral part of the SAP landscape. 

 The next future Is already taking shape 

 Over the years, SAP TechEd continually found new ways to bring technological developments to life and bring the SAP community together. New formats, greater interaction, and hands-on experiences had all helped shape the event. The community had long since become much more than an audience: it was an essential part of what made SAP TechEd what it was. 

 Then came 2020. “The global pandemic suddenly took away so much of what we had come to take for granted,” Kessler said. “SAP TechEd still took place, but it went digital. There were no exhibition halls where people could meet, no spontaneous reunions or conversations in the corridors, no discussions after a session that unexpectedly sparked a new idea.” 

 Hands-on experiences and exchanges with others had to take place under entirely different conditions. Something that had grown over many years could not simply be replicated online, one-to-one. “That’s when we realized just how much SAP TechEd depends on personal interaction,” Kessler recalled. 

 One of Kessler’s most memorable experiences shows how important that interaction was, even behind the scenes: the “speaker ready room.” Every year, around 130 speakers gathered in a large ballroom during SAP TechEd week to prepare for their sessions and help one another out. If they ran into problems with connectivity, licenses, updates, or integrating different components, they worked together to find solutions—often on the spot and under time pressure. 

 Over the years, this gave rise to a speaker community made up of familiar faces and newcomers who worked alongside SAP IT and the event organizers to make SAP TechEd happen. For Kessler, the ready room embodies the event’s distinctive sense of teamwork. Everyone wanted the sessions to succeed and participants to have the best possible experience. The shared mindset was simple: we’ll make it work—together. 

 In 2026, SAP TechEd finds itself at another technological turning point. Artificial intelligence is changing how software is developed, used and increasingly executed. Developers are working with AI-powered tools. Applications can take on tasks. Agents can execute processes and interact with one another. 

 “We have no more idea today of what will be commonplace 10 years from now than developers in 1996 could have known which of their futuristic ideas would eventually become standard practice,” Kessler said. “But that’s exactly the point. The future looked different at every SAP TechEd, yet the questions behind it have remained much the same: how can technology better support people? How can systems work together? How can we make complex processes simpler? What becomes possible when technical boundaries are pushed?” 
 SAP TechEd Berlin 2025 

 So, what connects the old hands attending their 30th SAP TechEd with the young talents joining for the first time in 2026? 

 Kessler’s answer is simple: “We all want to know what comes next—and discover together what’s possible.”

items.title: Blog 9 - SAP ESM for HR - UAT: How to Test SAP ESM for HR Before You Go Live
items.author: andreamazzanti
items.text:
The Phase That Always Gets Compressed 
 Ask any project manager on a delayed SAP ESM implementation what happens to the UAT phase when the schedule slips, and you will get the same answer: it gets compressed. Scope gets reduced, test cycles get shortened, defects get deferred, and teams convince themselves that what does not get tested in UAT will get caught in production. 
 It will. And it will be far more expensive to fix. 
 UAT — User Acceptance Testing — is the last structured opportunity to validate that everything you have designed, configured, and integrated actually works as intended, end to end, in a realistic environment, with real HR scenarios. It is not a technical check. It is a business validation. And done well, it is what separates a confident go-live from a nervous one. 
 This post gives you the framework to do it well. 
 What UAT in ESM Is — and What It Is No 
 A common mistake is treating ESM UAT as a feature checklist: "Can I create a case? Can I close a case? Can I search the knowledge base?" That approach will pass most scenarios and miss most of the real risks. 
 UAT for SAP ESM for HR is the validation of **end-to-end workflows** across all configured channels, categories, routing rules, SLA timers, integrations, and user roles, under realistic conditions, performed by the people who will use the system on day one. 
 The question you are answering is not "does the system work?" It is: "does the system work the way our HR operation needs it to, for every scenario that will arrive on day one?" 
 That is a materially different test. 
 Who Needs to Be in the UAT Team 
 UAT is not an IT activity. It is a joint business and IT activity, and the business must lead it. 
 The UAT team for an ESM for HR implementation should include: 
 | Role | Responsibility in UAT | 
 | **HR Agents (Tier 1)** | Test case creation, routing receipt, case processing, response templates, SLA visibility | 
 | **HR Specialists (Tier 2)** | Test escalated case handling, complex category workflows, direct-to-Tier-2 routing | 
 | **HR Managers / Supervisors** | Test supervisor views, SLA dashboards, escalation notifications, team workload visibility | 
 | **IT / Integration team** | Test SuccessFactors data validation, outbound transaction execution, IAS/SSO, BTP connectivity | 
 | **Employees (pilot group)** | Test the self-service portal, case submission, status tracking, email acknowledgement receipt | 
 | **UAT Coordinator** | Manages the test script, logs defects, tracks sign-off, coordinates the go/no-go decision | 
 The employee pilot group is the component most commonly omitted from UAT. This is a significant gap. HR agents can test the agent workspace all day, but only an actual employee can validate what the self-service experience feels like — whether the portal is navigable, whether the category options make sense, and whether the confirmation emails are clear. 
 Minimum recommended pilot group size: 10–15 employees drawn from different countries, departments, and seniority levels if your rollout is global. 
 The Five Test Scenario Types 
 A well-structured ESM for HR UAT covers five distinct scenario types. Each tests a different layer of the implementation. Missing any one of them leaves a class of risk untested. 
 Scenario Type 1 — Case Creation by Channel 
 What you are testing: That every configured inbound channel correctly creates a case, assigns it the right category, applies the right employee context, and routes it to the right team. 
 Test scenarios to include: 
 Employee submits a case via the self-service portal (standard category, correct country) 
 Employee emails the **HR mailbox** — case auto-creates with correct subject mapping and employee lookup 
 HR agent manually creates a case on behalf of an employee (walk-in / phone call scenario) 
 Employee uses SAP Joule — question answered from knowledge base (deflection success), and question not answered — case created automatically (deflection failure → case creation) 
 What to look for: 
 Does the employee's SuccessFactors profile load correctly in the case context? 
 Is the auto-acknowledgement email sent within the configured time (best practice: 5 minutes)? 
 Does the case land in the correct Agent Group queue? 
 Is the category pre-populated correctly for email-created cases? 
 Scenario Type 2 — Routing Validation 
 What you are testing: That every case category routes to the correct HR team, under every combination of employee country and org unit that is in scope. 
 This is the most labour-intensive scenario type because it requires you to test the routing matrix — every category × every country combination — not just a representative sample. Routing errors are silent in the system: the case creates without error, it just lands with the wrong team. 
 Test scenarios to include: 
 Same category submitted by employees in three different countries — verify different Agent Group assignment 
 Category that should route directly to Tier 2 (e.g., Employee Relations) — verify it bypasses Tier 1 entirely 
 Category submitted by an indirect employee (non-SuccessFactors EC) — verify fallback routing behaviour 
 Case submitted outside business hours — verify correct handling (queued, auto-reply, or out-of-hours team) 
 What to look for: 
 Does every category × country combination route to the expected team? 
 Is the direct-to-Tier-2 routing behaving correctly for complex categories? 
 What happens when the routing rule finds no match? Is there a safe fallback? 
 Scenario Type 3 — SLA Configuration 
 What you are testing: That SLA timers start correctly, business hours are applied accurately, warning notifications fire at the configured threshold, and breach notifications trigger on time. 
 SLA testing is frequently under-tested because testers do not want to wait for real-time timers to expire. The solution is to use test SLA configurations with compressed timers (e.g., 5-minute resolution SLA instead of 8-hour) in the UAT environment — then revert to production values before go-live. 
 Test scenarios to include: 
 Create a case and verify the SLA milestone fields populate with the correct due timestamps 
 Let a case approach the warning threshold — verify the warning notification fires to the correct recipient 
 Let a case breach — verify the breach notification fires, and any configured escalation actions execute (reassignment, priority change, supervisor notification) 
 Create a case outside business hours — verify the SLA timer does not count non-business hours 
 Test a public holiday calendar — verify the SLA timer pauses correctly on a configured holiday 
 What to look for: 
 Do SLA milestone timestamps reflect the correct business hours calculation? 
 Do warning and breach notifications reach the right recipients? 
 Does the escalation action (reassignment, priority change) execute correctly at breach? 
 Are public holidays and time zones handled correctly for each in-scope country? 
 Scenario Type 4 — SAP SuccessFactors Integration 
 What you are testing: That the integration between ESM and SuccessFactors works correctly in both directions — inbound employee data validation and outbound transaction automation. 
 This is the highest-risk scenario type in terms of go-live impact. An integration failure on day one affects every case, not just edge cases. 
 Test scenarios to include: 
 Submit a case as an active employee — verify the full SuccessFactors employee profile loads in the case context (name, employee ID, country, company code, org unit, manager, employment status) 
 Submit a case using an inactive employee ID — verify the system handles the lookup gracefully (error message, fallback behaviour) 
 If outbound transactions are in scope: trigger an automated HR transaction from a case (e.g., address change, leave request) — verify the transaction executes correctly in SuccessFactors and the case is updated with the outcome 
 Verify SSO: log in as an employee via the self-service portal — confirm no separate login is required 
 Verify IAS role propagation: log in as each user role (employee, HR agent, HR supervisor, HR administrator) — confirm each sees only what they should see and can perform only the actions they should be able to perform 
 What to look for: 
 Is the employee data lookup fast enough to be acceptable in production? (More than 3 seconds is a usability concern) 
 Are all expected SuccessFactors fields visible in the ESM case context? 
 Do outbound transactions execute without errors, and are they reflected correctly in SuccessFactors? 
 Does SSO work without prompting for credentials? 
 Scenario Type 5 — End-to-End Lifecycle 
 What you are testing: The full lifecycle of an HR case — from submission by an employee, through routing, agent processing, escalation if needed, resolution, employee notification, and case closure — across several representative scenarios. 
 This is the most important test type because it validates the system as a whole, not its individual components. It is also the scenario type most likely to surface integration and configuration gaps that were not visible in isolated tests. 
 Representative end-to-end scenarios to include: 
 Standard query resolved at Tier 1: 
 Employee submits payslip query via portal → routed to Payroll team → HR agent responds → employee receives notification → case closed → CSAT survey sent (if configured) 
 Query escalated from Tier 1 to Tier 2: 
 Employee submits query via email → Tier 1 agent reviews and escalates → case reassigned to Tier 2 specialist → specialist resolves → employee notified → case closed 
 Direct-to-Tier-2 complex case: 
 Employee submits an Employee Relations query → routes directly to ER specialist → specialist processes → case closed with internal notes 
 SLA breach scenario: 
 Case created → not actioned within SLA window → warning fires → breach occurs → escalation notification sent to supervisor → supervisor reassigns → case resolved 
 Joule deflection scenario: 
 Employee asks a question via Joule → answer provided from knowledge base → no case created → employee confirms resolved 
 How to Structure Your UAT Script 
 A UAT script is more than a list of steps. Each test case should contain six elements: 
 | Element | Description | 
 | **Test Case ID** | Unique identifier (e.g., UAT-CH-001 for channel tests) | 
 | **Scenario Description** | Plain-language description of what is being tested and why | 
 | **Prerequisites** | What must be true before the test can start (user logged in, test employee ID available, etc.) | 
 | **Step-by-step test actions** | Exactly what the tester does, in sequence | 
 | **Expected result** | Precisely what the system should do — not "it works" but "case routes to Payroll EMEA Agent Group within 30 seconds with employee profile loaded" | 
 | **Pass / Fail / Deferred** | The outcome, with space for the tester to add notes | 
 The level of precision in the expected result is what separates a useful UAT script from a useless one. "System behaves correctly" is not an expected result. "Case appears in the Payroll EMEA Agent Group queue within 60 seconds, with employee name, employee ID, and country populated from SuccessFactors EC" is. 
 Defect Classification: What Is a Blocker? 
 Not every defect found in UAT should block go-live. The decision about what to fix before go-live and what to defer requires a clear classification framework. Use a three-tier approach: 
 P1 — Go-live blocker: 
 Any defect that prevents a case from being created, routed, or processed 
 Any SSO or IAS failure that prevents users from accessing the system 
 Any SuccessFactors integration failure that causes incorrect employee data 
 Any SLA misconfiguration that causes incorrect due dates 
 Any routing error that sends cases to the wrong team 
 P2 — Fix before go-live, non-blocking: 
 Notification email formatting issues 
 Minor UI/label discrepancies 
 Knowledge base article content errors 
 Non-critical re

items.text: What if any business user could query SAP data in plain English no transaction codes, no ABAP, no SQL? In this post, I walk through a reusable MCP pattern that exposes standard SAP tables as natural-language-accessible tools inside Joule Work Desktop and Joule Work Zone custom agents. The architecture is simpler than you'd expect, and the pattern applies far beyond the use case we built it for.

items.title: From process mining to action: What's new in the Process Consulting Agent October release
items.author: Patrizia_Calvia
items.text:
SAP Signavio's Process Consulting Agent empowers you to analyze processes, surface insights, and drive transformation initiatives, all through natural language conversation. 
 Process improvement has always been the domain of specialists: analysts who know their way around event logs, SIGNAL queries, and dashboards, interpreting and retrieving findings manually. This depth of knowledge has been instrumental in surfacing valuable process insights for organizations. At the same time, the need for expert analytical skills has made process mining less accessible for business users without a technical background. The Process Consulting Agent changes that by putting expert-level process intelligence in everyone's hands. 
 Since its release in August, the Process Consulting Agent has continued to evolve to deliver deeper process mining capabilities while covering also the SAP Signavio Process Transformation Manager scope . 
 This means users can now seamlessly get a fully detailed process mining analysis, recommendations and structured visualizations and metrics, out of a business question, and then turn it into structured transformation initiatives, all in a single conversation. 

 Deeper process mining: analysis in seconds, not days 
 With the latest release, the Process Consulting Agent was enriched with process mining capabilities (generally available) including cycle time analysis, process variant exploration, throughput, conformance, and event-level details, all accessible through natural language. With these capabilities, it is significantly easier and less costly for analysts and business users to perform investigations that previously required deep expertise in SIGNAL queries. 
 Cycle time and throughput : Understand end-to-end durations, identify where time is lost between specific milestones, and track throughput trends over any period. 
 Rework and conformance : Surface rework loops, skipped steps, and deviations from the defined process path, automatically, not after the fact. 
 Process variants : Discover the distinct paths cases actually take through a process and compare them against the intended design. 
 All of this at event-level detail, drilling from fleet-wide KPIs down to the complete activity log of a single case. 
 This means a procurement manager can ask "Why did supplier invoice processing time spike last month?" and get a data-grounded answer in seconds. A process analyst can investigate regional performance differences in a single conversation, rather than building a report overnight. 
 Also, with the October suite release we are taking a much bigger step forward by introducing a beta program that allows you to move to a fully agent-led process mining experience via MCP. With the agent led mining MCP you can run the full analysis workflow, identify root causes using the automated root cause analysis engine, surface inefficiencies and obtain recommendations, all without manual intervention. 
 Importantly, the user remains at the center of the experience. The agent presents its findings transparently, showing the analysis it performed, the data it used, and the reasoning behind its conclusions, so users can validate, challenge, and refine the results iteratively. This is augmented intelligence, not a black box: the agent does the heavy lifting, but the human makes the decisions. 
 Process Transformation Manager integration (generally available) 
 Identifying a process problem is only half the work. Also critical is converting that finding into structured, trackable transformation activity, and doing so without losing the context that made the recommendation meaningful in the first place. 
 The October release connects the Process Consulting Agent directly with SAP Signavio Process Transformation Manager. The Process Consulting Agent provides an overview of existing transformation initiatives and their status, helping users understand what is already in progress before creating or updating transformation work. 
 When the agent surfaces an improvement opportunity, users can act on it: 
 Create transformation initiatives directly from agent recommendations , pre-populated with the opportunity description, rationale, affected process area, and suggested next steps, with no need for manual recreation. 
 Capture process findings as structured insights and link them to the relevant initiative , keeping the analytical evidence connected to the transformation work. 
 Reduce duplicate effort: the agent can reference existing transformation initiatives so new recommendations are aligned with ongoing work rather than generated in isolation. 
 The integration also extends to value management. The Process Consulting Agent can create Value Cases in SAP Signavio Process Transformation Manager based on insights generated by the agent or business inputs provided by users, helping teams connect identified improvement opportunities to expected business value and prioritize accordingly. 
 The result: the path from "here is what the data shows" to "here is the initiative we are running to fix it" compresses from weeks to a single conversation and full transparency on transformation work. 
 The Bigger Picture 
 These two enhancements reflect the same underlying goal: making expert-level process analysis and transformation management accessible to anyone, while freeing expert users to focus on higher-value activities. Process owners get answers on demand. Analysts spend less time on data extraction and manual analysis, and more time on decision-making. Transformation leads can move faster, with recommendation context preserved throughout. 
 The Process Consulting Agent is one of two agents within the Process Transformation Assistant. Alongside the Process Data Modeling Agent , now in beta in labs for the engagement layer of your choice such as Copilot, Claude, Joule Work Desktop, they cover complementary parts of the process transformation lifecycle: the Process Data Modeling Agent automates most of the workflow to set up ready-to-mine object-centric process data models, while the Process Consulting Agent performs analysis, derives insights and recommendations and converts findings into transformation initiatives at ease. 
 Expected in November 2026 , the Process Consulting Agent will extend its reach to SAP Signavio Process Modeler , further broadening its scope and the value it can deliver across the full SAP Signavio Process Transformation Suite (The embedded video delivers a preview). 
 Start your journey today 
 Activate the Process Consulting Agent and experience a new way to investigate your processes. And if you want to be first in line for what comes next, apply to our beta programs in SAP Signavio Lab Space (mail: signavio_lab_space@sap.com) 
 Want to know what else is coming out as part of this release? Check out our highlight blog for SAP Signavio Process Transformation Suite and find out what else we have coming out this month!

items.title: SAP Ariba Source to Contract 2611 Release Key Innovations Preview
items.author: HoangD
items.text:
Hey SAP Community! 
 The 2611 release is right around the corner, and I wanted to give you a heads-up on some of the things our teams have been working on across Strategic Sourcing, Strategic Contracts, and Public Sector Sourcing. 
 Honestly? A lot of this release is about fixing friction. Not big flashy features — just the stuff that slows people down in their daily work. I think you'll recognize a few of these. 
 Let's walk through them. 

 SAP Ariba Strategic Sourcing 
 Ability to Edit Decimal Place Limits in Terms for All Items 
 You can finally update decimal place limits for multiple items at once instead of doing it one by one. 
 If you've ever set up a sourcing event with dozens of line items and had to configure each one individually, you already know why this matters. It's one of those changes that won't make headlines but will absolutely save your team time every single time you set up an event. 

 Enhancements to the Grading Comments Capability in Guided Sourcing 
 Grading comments in guided sourcing now support attachments. Both the Consensus grading page and the Grade as a team member page. 
 This came up a lot in customer conversations — teams were writing paragraphs in comments trying to describe a document or reference a scorecard, when really they just needed to attach a file. Now they can. It's a small addition but it makes the whole grading experience feel a lot more complete. 

 Sync Latest Supplier Qualification Status in Guided Sourcing Events 
 Picture this: you're deep into an evaluation and awarding process, and you find out a supplier's qualification status changed after you pulled them into the event. Your event is showing old data. What do you do? 
 Until now, there wasn't a great answer. With 2611, you can manually trigger a sync of qualification status from Supplier Management directly into the event. One action, and you're working with current data again. It sounds simple because it is — but it makes a real difference when you're trying to make confident award decisions. 

 Prevent Award Submission for Suppliers Not Configured in SAP Master Data Governance 
 For teams running SAP Master Data Governance, this one's about catching a problem before it becomes a problem. If a supplier isn't set up in MDG, the system will now block the award submission right then and there — rather than letting it go through and creating a mess downstream. 
 It's a guardrail, plain and simple. And if you've ever had to untangle an MDG-related data issue after an award already went through, you know exactly why this matters. 

 Ability to Add Article Master Items in Guided Sourcing 
 This one closes a gap that's been bothering a few of our customers for a while. If you needed to kick off master data creation for an item in a guided sourcing event, you had to leave the event to do it. That's disruptive, and it happens at a point in the process where you really don't want to be jumping between screens. 
 Starting with 2611, you can trigger that master data creation flow directly from the Items table — right there in the Monitor phase, without going anywhere else. And it works the same way no matter how the item got into the event. Consistent, in-context, done. 

 Ability to Reopen ETendering Events 
 Public sector procurement doesn't leave a lot of room for improvisation — which is how it should be. But sometimes something happens after an eTendering event closes that genuinely requires a do-over, and teams have needed a proper way to handle that. 
 Now event administrators can reopen an ET event as a defined exception procedure. It's controlled, it's auditable, and it gives public sector teams an official mechanism for situations that used to require awkward workarounds. 

 Running Bid History Reports in the Background for Large Supplier Responses 
 If you run high-volume sourcing events, you've been there — waiting on a bid history report to finish generating while 100+ supplier responses churn through the system. It's a lot of time to just sit there. 
 Starting in 2611, when an event has more than 100 supplier responses, the report runs in the background. You get notified when it's ready. Go do something else in the meantime. It's a practical fix for a real frustration, and I think teams running large-scale sourcing events are going to feel this one quickly. 

 SAP Ariba Contract Management 
 Quick Access to Supplier Engagement Details from Contract Workspaces 
 OK this one is genuinely one of my favorites in the release, and it's not complicated at all. When you're in a contract workspace and you need to check the related supplier engagement, the engagement request ID is now a link. Click it, you're there. 
 And when you're done on the engagement details page, there's a back link that takes you straight back to the contract workspace. That's it. It sounds almost too simple to call out, but if you regularly move between contracts and engagements, you've felt this pain. No more hunting. 
 --- 
 As always, these feature updates will go live with the 2611 release. Once published, you can use the official feature IDs on help.sap.com for deeper technical documentation. Stay tuned for our additional upcoming blog posts and follow me to stay informed on upcoming feature releases across SAP Ariba. 
 Thank you for being a part of the SAP Ariba community and we look forward to continuing our journey of innovation together!

items.title: I taught SAP RPT-1.6 to play Tetris
items.author: Florian2024
items.text:
SAP RPT-1.6 is a tabular foundation model. It does not chat and it does not generate text. You give it a table in which some cells say [PREDICT] , and it fills them in, using the other rows of the same table as examples. That is all it does. 
 Inspired by the LinkedIn post of Philipp Herzig showing RPT 1.6 playing Snake against Jev, I asked a playful question: can a model that only knows how to complete tables play Tetris? Not with a Tetris model trained for weeks, but with the stock model on SAP AI Core, the same model you would use to predict delivery delays or payment dates. 
 It can. Over two 100-piece games, RPT-1.6 cleared 38 and 35 lines. The hand-tuned heuristic it learned from cleared 38 and 39. No weights were changed. Everything RPT knows about Tetris arrives in the request, as 64 example rows per move. 
 This post explains how that works: how a game move becomes a table, what goes into the context, and why a table model can make good moves at all.
